analysis.title: MasTec Inc. (MTZ): Announces Agreement to Acquire Murphy Corporation; Strengthens Prefabrication and Exposure to High-Growth End-Markets
key_insights: MTZ announced before market open on 11/20/2026 that it will acquire Murphy Corporation, a mechanical contractor with engineering, preconstruction and prefabrication expertise, for about $1.25 bil in cash.
A potential earnout payment depends on Murphy's cumulative 3-year financial performance after closing. The deal will be financed with a bank term loan and is expected to close expeditiously.

Murphy serves data centers, healthcare, aviation and defense, and pharmaceutical manufacturing, and provides recurring maintenance services. MTZ frames the deal as strengthening its prefabrication and construction expertise.

Per the release, Murphy is expected to generate about $775 mil revenue and about $140 mil adjusted EBITDA in 2026. That implies an EBITDA margin near 18% and a purchase price near 8.9x 2026 adjusted EBITDA, computed from the stated figures.
MTZ expects the deal to be accretive to revenue, adjusted EBITDA, EPS and cash flow from operations immediately after closing.
Pro forma net leverage after closing will be about 2.7x, with MTZ expecting it to fall below 2.0x in 2027.
GS keeps its Buy rating and $274 12-month price target, based on 12.0x NTM EV/EBITDA. The stock closed at $164.76 on 19 Nov 2026, which implies 66.3% upside.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps its Buy and $274 target on a 12.0x NTM EV/EBITDA multiple after the Murphy acquisition announcement. The price target is unchanged from 21-Oct-26.

earnings_insights: Murphy Corporation 2026 expected revenue is about $775 mil and adjusted EBITDA about $140 mil, per the MTZ release (company-stated expectation, not a reported result).

GS EPS estimates for MTZ: $9.33 for 12/26E, $10.28 for 12/27E and $11.56 for 12/28E, against $6.55 for 12/25. Quarterly GS estimates: $3.03 for 9/26E, $2.69 for 12/26E and $1.61 for 3/27E. The 6/26 quarter shows $2.22.
MTZ expects the Murphy deal to be accretive to EPS immediately after closing.
risk_factors: A persistent decline in Renewable energy-related backlog.
Pro forma net leverage of about 2.7x after the cash-funded, term-loan-financed deal.
